title: Unified Inference: Q4 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates the Q4 2026 product overview, PRD (requirements and success criteria), design specs, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments). It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and support teams executing the Q4 release and subsequent rollouts.

Quick summary:
- Goal: Ship Unified Inference v7 feature set with predictable latency SLOs, cost-saving optimizer controls, and simplified pricing tiers for enterprise customers.
- Scope: API surface changes (batching/streaming controls), runtime changes (cache-aware batching, quantization profiles), new pricing tiers, and migration + rollout guidance.
- Target release window: 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-20 (staged canary -> regional rollout).

1) Product goals and success metrics:
- Business goals:
  - Increase conversion for Dedicated contracts by 20% YoY via clearer pricing and predictable throughput guarantees.
  - Reduce average per-token cost for mid-tier customers by 15% via Redwood Optimize integration.
- Product success metrics (SLOs):
  - 95th percentile request latency (text generation, 512 tokens) <= 120ms for hosted API in us-west-2.
  - Token throughput increase: 1.3x on average for typical RLHF prompt distributions after batching & cache improvements.
  - Reduction in model fallback incidents by 60% due to improved routing and variant compatibility checks.

2) Audience and use cases:
- Primary: product engineers and ML engineers building LLM features (chat, completion, embeddings, reranking).
- Secondary: platform teams purchasing Dedicated capacity and enterprises evaluating Private deployments.
- Use cases prioritized: real-time chat (latency-first), bulk embedding pipelines (throughput-first), RAG (cost-quality tradeoff).

3) Requirements (user stories & system requirements):
User stories (must-have):
1. As a developer, I can set per-route latency and cost targets so requests automatically route to a model variant that meets the target.
2. As an SRE, I can define a canary rollout policy that gradually increases traffic to v7 across regions and reverts automatically on error budget breach.
3. As a platform admin, I can pin a model version and quantization profile per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments.

System requirements (MUST):
- Runtime must support prefix KV caching and workload-aware batching configurable per-route.
- API must expose new per-request hints: {"latency_target_ms", "cost_tier", "quality_floor"}. Example: {"latency_target_ms":100, "cost_tier":2}.
- Redwood Optimize integration: autosuggest quantization profile and batching config with recommended savings estimate (tokens/sec and $/1M tokens).
- Observability: per-route token latency histogram, per-model quantization leakage alerting, token-level cost breakdown retained for 30 days.

Non-functional requirements:
- Hosted API 99.9% uptime SLA for production endpoints.
- Dedicated: contractual throughput and p99 latency within 10% of hosted baseline.
- Security: private deployments must integrate with customer KMS/HSM and support audit-logging for inference requests.

4) Design specs (high-level):
Architecture changes:
- Smart routing layer (routing-engine v2):
  - Inputs: per-request hints, user-configured policies, region & tier.
  - Decision tree: latency-first -> route to low-latency quantized model variant; cost-first -> route to high-batch-friendly quantized variant; fallback -> model variants ranked by compatibility and quality score.
- Runtime v7 changes:
  - Cache-aware batching: batching algorithm uses per-customer KV cache hit ratio to prioritize requests that can reuse KV to reduce compute.
  - Kernel selection: expand kernel table to include int8 and nf4 profiles on A100/H100/Inferentia classes.
  - KV cache size autoscaler with heuristics: cache_size = min(32GB, 0.1 * total_active_kv_size).

API changes (backwards-compatible):
- New optional fields in /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints (examples):
  - latency_target_ms (int)
  - cost_tier (int: 1=low,2=balanced,3=high-quality)
  - quality_floor (float 0..1): soft constraint used by routing to avoid variants expected to drop below quality threshold.
Example request snippet (JSON):
{
  "model": "redwood-unified-7",
  "input": "Summarize the following...",
  "latency_target_ms": 100,
  "cost_tier": 2,
  "quality_floor": 0.95
}

Config and defaults (table-like text):
- Default latency_target_ms: 200ms for chat; 500ms for batch generation.
- Default cost_tier: 2 (balanced).
- Fallback policy: 3-step (same-region variant -> cross-region compatible -> degrade to cached response if configured).

5) Roadmap & themes (quarterly roadmap items):
Q4 2026 (release window):
- Feature-complete API + runtime v7; Redwood Optimize autosuggestions GA; pricing tier updates; canary rollouts start.
- Deliverables: public API spec, SDK updates (python/node/java), Dedicated capacity SKU definitions, Private deployment installer changes, console dashboards for per-route SLOs.
Q1 2027:
- Expand model catalog to include additional open models with verified performance profiles.
- Deeper integrations with third-party KMS and SIEM tools.

Cross-cutting themes:
- Developer-first: clear SDKs, migration helpers, and docs with example prompts.
- Cost transparency: token-level cost breakdown and sim-mode for expected monthly bill.
- Reliability: robust fallbacks and automated rollback on error budget breaches.

6) Pricing & packaging notes:
New pricing structure (effective 2026-12-05):
- Hosted API tiers:
  - Starter (S): $0.002 / 1K tokens (best effort latency), intended for prototyping.
  - Standard (M): $0.01 / 1K tokens (balanced latency & cost), includes Redwood Optimize suggestions.
  - Enterprise (L): Custom per-token pricing with SLA and dedicated support; includes Dedicated-friendly discounts and reserved capacity options.
- Dedicated: monthly committed capacity (examples):
  - Bronze: 2 reserved GPUs (approx. 250M tokens / month), baseline support, $8,000/month.
  - Silver: 8 reserved GPUs, 1.2B tokens/month, enhanced SLAs, $28,000/month.
  - Gold: custom sizing, reserved throughput SLAs, enterprise support.
- Private: licensing + installation fee + annual support; pricing quoted per customer.

Discounting and add-ons:
- Reserved + committed usage discounts available (10-35% depending on term).
- Observability retention add-on (token-level cost & latency history beyond 30 days).

Pricing examples (illustrative):
- Mid-market app (Standard tier): 200M tokens/month => ~$2,000/month before any committed discounts and caching savings.
- Dedicated Bronze customer: baseline 250M tokens/month, typical billed unit cost ~25-40% lower than hosted Standard after batching & caching.

7) Migration and compatibility guidance:
Migration steps for customers pinned to older APIs: (numbered rollout)
1. Announce v7 availability and compatibility matrix via release notes and console banner.
2. Offer migration guide and automated migration tool in SDK to add latency_target_ms and cost_tier hints.
3. Encourage customers to run sim-mode (console) for 2 weeks to view expected cost/latency changes.
4. For Dedicated/Private: coordinate on a dry-run in a staging cluster, confirm KMS integration, and schedule a cutover window with traffic mirroring for 48 hours.

API compatibility table (text):
- /v1/generate: backward compatible. New fields optional.
- Streaming contract unchanged.
- If quality_floor is set and not achievable, routing-engine returns HTTP 409 with a suggested alternative and reason.

8) Release notes (notable changes in v7):
- Core improvements:
  - Runtime v7: cache-aware batching and expanded int8/nf4 kernel support (A100/H100/Inferentia).
  - Routing-engine v2: latency/cost-target aware routing with automatic variant fallback.
  - Redwood Optimize GA: autosuggestions for batching and quantization profiles with estimated savings.
- API additions:
  - latency_target_ms, cost_tier, quality_floor on generate/chat endpoints.
  - New /v1/optimize/simulate endpoint (beta) to estimate savings for a given prompt set.
- Console/UI:
  - Per-route SLO controls, traffic simulators, and migration checklist.
- SDK updates:
  - python-sdk v3.2.0, node-sdk v2.8.0, java-sdk v1.9.0. Migration helpers included.

9) Rollout plan and canary policy (detailed):
- Canary cohorts: internal -> 1% external customers (low-risk) -> 10% region -> 50% region -> global. Each stage runs 24-72 hours and must pass: error-rate < 0.5% above baseline, no SLO regressions, and no critical perf regressions (p95).
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - Error rate increase > 0.5% for 30m
  - p95 latency regression > 25% for 30m
  - Model fallback rate > 1% sustained for 30m
- Rollout commands (devops example):
  - Start canary: rcli rollout start --service unified-inference --version v7 --cohort canary1
  - Promote: rcli rollout promote --service unified-inference --version v7 --percent 10
  - Abort & rollback: rcli rollout abort --service unified-inference --version v7 --to-version v6

10) Post-release monitoring and playbooks:
- Dashboards to monitor: per-route p50/p95/p99, token throughput, KV cache hit rate, model fallback rate, per-customer cost delta.
- Alerts (examples):
  - High fallback rate: fallback_rate > 1% for 5m -> P1 paging to infra-oncall.
  - Latency regression: p95 > SLA threshold for 10m -> P1.
- Incident playbook highlights:
  1. Identify affected route(s) and top-customer(s).
  2. Snapshot current runtime kernels and routing decisions.
  3. If needed, manually pin routing to previous model variant and abort rollout.

11) Ownership & contacts:
- Product lead: Maya Chen (product)
- Technical owner: Daniel Park (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE lead: Fiona Gallagher (eng-sre)

12) Rollback and postmortem expectations:
- For any rollback triggered during rollout, follow the oncall_and_incident_response/postmortems template and produce a postmortem within 5 business days. Root cause, mitigation, timeline, and action items required.

Appendix A — Example simulate request to /v1/optimize/simulate (text):
POST /v1/optimize/simulate
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-unified-7",
  "prompt_set_id": "proj-123-2026-q4",
  "metrics": ["latency", "cost"],
  "baseline": {"cost_tier": 2}
}

Expected response (summarized):
{
  "estimated_monthly_savings": "$1,250",
  "recommended_quantization": "nf4",
  "expected_p50_latency_ms": 95
}
